text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi rejected accusations of insider trading as he allegedly bought 50,000 Union Bank shares before the merger with North Estonian Bank was announced. Vaehi and Finance Minister Mart Opmann denied having bought any shares.

- The former chief of the Defence Forces General Staff Colonel Ants Laaneots, who retired in 1994 due to conflicts with then Defence Forces commander General Einseln, has returned to service as Defence Forces inspector general.

- The broadcasting licensing commission granted a TV license to the TV1 private station, which mainly broadcasts news. A channel oriented to a Russian-language audience is also planned by another firm, TV-COM. The decision on a license will be made in late January.

- The Estonian Institute for Market Research interviewed 17 experts, who rated Estonian economic growth in 1996 as 2.5 percent and are pessimistic about the coming year due to a high trade deficit and decreasing investments.
- Schoolteachers and authorities are ignoring violence among pupils, an article claims.
- Two organised crime figures from Narva in northeastern Estonia admitted to having distributed leaflets with anti-Russian texts in order to distract the security police.
- Parliament vice-chairman Arnold Ruutel rejected most of the benefits he is entitled to as ex-president and had them replaced by a sum of money he intends to use on scientific research.
- The lawyers' association granted the security police permission to bring charges against a lawyer accused of attempted bribing of a judge.
- The government rejected the draft law on minimum prices on agricultural products and plans to formulate an integrated agricultural policy.
